cards.subject: The second city of Lordaeron
lines: The northernmost and second most populous city of the kingdom. Alonsus Chapel, where the Order of the Silver Hand was founded, stood here.
Arthas purged it himself, and the fires he started are the fires still burning while you stand in the street.

cards.subject: Two doors, one saved run
lines: The Scarlet side and the Scourge side are the same instance and the same lockout — most groups only ever see one of them.
Come in the main gate and it closes.
The ways out are a hearthstone, a portal, or fighting all the way across the city to the other door.

cards.subject: He would not leave the shop
lines: He sold premium tobacco, and when the Scourge came he refused to abandon it.
He fought for his tobacco and he lost.
He is still standing behind his own counter.

cards.subject: He is modelled like the ordinary ghouls
lines: Groups walk into him by accident, in Market Row, because nothing about him looks different.
He announces himself by yelling "TIMMY!"
Underneath the joke: he traded atrocities for unholy power, and what is left of his mind answers to a childhood nickname he hated.

cards.subject: The wraith was one of Arthas's soldiers
lines: She was Lylia, "a blade of righteousness among her people".
At the culling she killed innocents by her own hand until her mind gave way, and then she killed herself.
She is still standing in the street where it happened.

cards.subject: There is a postal service
lines: Kill the Stratholme Courier and he drops three mailbox keys. Six mailboxes are scattered near the gates.
Every one you open spits out three elite Undead Postmen.
Open the third and the Postmaster turns up in person, with a retinue.

cards.subject: He exists because you bent down
lines: Blacksmithing plans turn up at random on the floor of the instance — on the ground before the Hoard, on a bench near the archive.
Reaching for them spawns him.
He is on no map and in no boss list. Picking up litter is the summon.

cards.subject: You get to burn the library
lines: He guards the Scarlet Crusade's archive, and when he dies there is a book left on his desk.
Click it and the whole archive goes up.
It is one of very few places in vanilla where the player is the one who burns something down.

cards.subject: The Grand Crusader is a dreadlord
lines: The man leading the Scarlet Crusade is not a man. Balnazzar killed the paladin Saidan Dathrohan and has been wearing him ever since.
He starts the fight in the human shape and sheds it partway through.
The Crusade's own commander is the thing it exists to fight.

cards.subject: One in five thousand
lines: The Baron's skeletal horse dropped at roughly two hundredths of one percent in vanilla.
It was raised to one percent in patch 3.0.2, three expansions later.
Every Baron run in this game was also a lottery ticket at those odds.

cards.subject: The clock is for her
lines: The timed run is not "kill the Baron". It is engage him — pull him inside the window and the clock is satisfied.
Run out of time and he executes her in front of you: "None shall defy the Scourge and live!"
Hers: "My death means nothing... light... will prevail!"

cards.subject: One crusader comes with you
lines: A medallion sits in a locked strongbox on the Scarlet side. Give it to Aurius and he walks out of his sanctuary and fights the Baron at your shoulder.
He does not survive it.
"I'll die here, but because of you... I'll die in peace."

cards.subject: There is a raid portal that goes nowhere
lines: An unused portal stands in the square where the Baron's abominations pace.
It was going to be the original way into Naxxramas — you would have walked into the necropolis through this city, the way you walk into Molten Core through Blackrock Depths.
It was never wired up.
